title: Choosing an Executor Worksheet
description: Questions to help you decide who should settle your estate, plus a backup, before you name them in your will.
intro: Your executor handles the paperwork, bills, and family questions after you die. The job can take months and calls for patience. Use these questions to compare the people you are considering.

sections.heading: Skills and temperament
items: Is this person organized and good at following through on paperwork?
Are they comfortable dealing with banks, courts, and government agencies?
Do they stay calm under pressure and during family disagreements?
Are they honest and careful with other people's money?

sections.heading: Availability
items: Do they have the time to handle months of tasks and phone calls?
Where do they live, and does your state add rules for out-of-state executors?
How is their health, and how old are they compared to you?
Would they be willing to serve if asked today?

sections.heading: Family dynamics
items: Would naming this person cause tension among your children or relatives?
Is this person also a beneficiary, and could that create a conflict?
Would co-executors work well together, or slow things down?
Would a professional executor or trust company be a better fit?

sections.heading: Estate complexity
items: Does your estate include a business, rental property, or out-of-state real estate?
Will the executor need to sell a house or manage investments?
Are there likely to be tax filings beyond a final income tax return?
Have you reviewed the executor workload tool to see the tasks involved?

sections.heading: Next steps
items: Choose a first choice and at least one backup
Ask each person if they are willing to serve
Tell your executor where your will and asset inventory are kept
Name your executor and backups in your will
